paper.title: Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
paper.shortTitle: Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
paper.authors: HerringtonWilliam G., StaplinNatalie, WannerChristoph et al.

thesis: Empagliflozin reduced the risk of the composite outcome of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death in a wide range of patients at risk of CKD progression.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What effect or association is supported in the studied human population?

nodes.title: Choose cohort and endpoint
nodes.body: We randomly assigned 6609 participants to empagliflozin (10mg once daily) versus matching placebo.

nodes.title: Measure human outcomes
nodes.body: This study, the EMPA-KIDNEY trial, was designed to assess the effects of empagliflozin in a broad range of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) at risk of progression.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: There were fewer hospitalizations from any cause in the empagliflozin group (0.86; 0.78 to 0.95, P=0.003), but no statistically significant effect on hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death (4.0% vs 4.6%), or death from any cause (4.5% vs 5.1%).

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: Empagliflozin reduced the risk of the composite outcome of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death in a wide range of patients at risk of CKD progression.
